for `"2100-02-28"` to `"2100-03-01"`. Dates in 2024 and 2000 look fine.

The bug is obvious: `is_leap` only checks `year % 4 == 0`, and ignores the century-year rule (which its own docstring even mentions). Let's check the truncated middle portion of the file:

The rest of the code (`days_in_month`, `ordinal`, `days_between`) all correctly delegate to `is_leap`, so the only fix needed is to implement the Gregorian century rule that the docstring already describes:
Now verify with the test suite and a few extra sanity checks:

from isodate import days_between, is_leap
assert is_leap(2024) and is_leap(2000)
assert not is_leap(1900) and not is_leap(2100) and not is_leap(2104) or is_leap(2104)
assert is_leap(2104)
assert days_between("1900-02-28", "1900-03-01") == 1
assert days_between("2100-02-28", "2100-03-01") == 1
assert days_between("2024-02-28", "2024-03-01") == 2
assert days_between("2000-02-28", "2000-03-01") == 2
assert days_between("2024-03-01", "2024-02-28") == -2
assert days_between("1900-01-01", "1901-01-01") == 365
assert days_between("2000-01-01", "2001-01-01") == 366
assert days_between("2100-01-01", "2101-01-01") == 365
assert days_between("1899-12-31", "1900-01-01") == 1

    days_between("1900-02-29", "1900-03-01")
    raise AssertionError("1900-02-29 should be invalid")
except ValueError:

try:
    days_between("2000-02-29", "2000-03-01")  # valid, 2000 is a leap year
except ValueError:
    raise AssertionError("2000-02-29 should be valid")

content: All tests pass and the sanity checks confirm the fix. Submitting.

arguments.summary: Fixed the off-by-one in `days_between` around century Februaries by correcting `is_leap` in `isodate/dates.py`. It previously returned `year % 4 == 0`, which wrongly treated 1900 and 2100 as leap years (giving February 29 days and an extra day in the ordinal count). It now implements the full Gregorian rule the docstring already described: `year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)`. Since `days_in_month`, `parse_date`, and `ordinal` all delegate to `is_leap`, this single-line change fixes `days_between("1900-02-28", "1900-03-01")` and the 2100 case (both now return 1), keeps 2000/2024 correct, and additionally makes `1900-02-29` properly invalid. No new dependencies were added, per the maintainer's requirement; the test suite passes.
